summary: Steffen Döll is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his M.A. and doctorate at the University of Munich, also studying at Kyoto University. His career includes posts at Munich, Kyoto, and the University of Hamburg, where he became Numata Professor in 2015.

Steingrímur Bjarnason Thorsteinsson was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Menntaskólinn í Reykjavík and the University of Copenhagen, later serving as a teacher and senior teacher at Menntaskólinn í Reykjavík from 1872.

Stella Kramrisch was an Indologist and art historian who earned her Ph.D. at the University of Vienna under Josef Strzygowski and Max Dvořák. She held major posts at Calcutta, Visva-Bharati, the Philadelphia Museum of Art, New York University, and the University of Pennsylvania.
Stella Sandahl is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied under Armand Minard. She held an academic post at the University of Toronto, attested in 1984.

Sten Konow was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Oslo and completed his Ph.D. at Halle under Richard Pischel, later holding chairs at the University of Hamburg and the University of Oslo.

Stephan Licha works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. After earning his Ph.D. from SOAS University of London, he completed postdoctoral positions at Waseda University and the University of Tokyo before joining the faculty at the University of Chicago.

Stephan Marcus Salzberg is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of British Columbia, where his teachers included Yoshitaka Iriya, Shoko Kanaoka, and Daniel L. Overmyer.

Stephan V. Beyer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Rochester and under Richard Hugh Robinson, later serving as a professor at the University of Wisconsin–Madison from approximately 1972 to 1980.

Stephanie Kaza is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oberlin, Stanford, UC Santa Cruz, and Starr King School for the Ministry. She served as an assistant professor and professor emeritus at the University of Vermont.
Stephanie Roemer is a scholar in the field of Tibetology. She completed her doctoral studies under supervisors Eberhard Sandschneider and Toni Huber.

Stephanie W. Jamison is an Indologist, linguist, and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies who completed her doctorate at Yale under Stanley Insler and Warren Crawford Cowgill. She taught at Harvard and became Professor of Sanskrit at UCLA around 2002.

Stephen Addiss was a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history. He earned degrees from Harvard and the University of Michigan, subsequently holding professorships at the University of Kansas (1977–1992) and the University of Richmond (1992–2013).

Stephen Batchelor works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Songgwangsa, the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, and Tibet Institute Rikon under teachers including Geshe Rabten, and later directed Sharpham College and taught at Bodhi College.

Stephen C. Berkwitz is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Vermont, University of Kelaniya, and UC Santa Barbara (Ph.D. 1999). In 1999, he became Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Missouri State University.

Stephen F. Teiser specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Oberlin College and Princeton University under Alan Sponberg, Denis Twitchett, and Daniel L. Overmyer, later becoming D. T. Suzuki Professor in Buddhist Studies at Princeton.

Stephen Fuchs was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Wilhelm Schmidt and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna. He taught at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, and directed the Institute of Indian Culture.

Stephen G. Covell is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his doctoral studies under Jacqueline I. Stone at Princeton University and joined the faculty at Western Michigan University around 2001.
Stephen H. Phillips is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He served as a professor of philosophy and later professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin.

Stephen Harris is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of New Mexico in 2014 and was appointed Assistant Professor at Leiden University that same year.
Stephen Hislop was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Glasgow and the University of Edinburgh, earning an M.A., and studied under Thomas Chalmers.
